subject: Cumulus Health RFI: inference network containment & isolation details
messages:
From: Alex Byrne <alex.byrne@cumulus-health.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security.team@cumulus-health.com
Date: Mon, 22 May 2028 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: network containment and tenant isolation for inference workloads

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for agreeing to take our security questionnaire. Our security and network teams have a focused set of follow-ups on how Redwood contains inference workloads at the network and tenancy level. High-level asks:

1) A concise network diagram showing trust zones for hosted vs. dedicated vs. private deployment models (include egress paths).
2) Explanation of how tenant traffic is isolated at the hyperplane / serving runtime layer — specifically KV-cache handling and cross-tenant memory isolation.
3) Threat scenarios and mitigations for lateral movement originating from compromised managed-control-plane components.

We'd like something we can annotate and include in our internal review by next Thursday. If you have a one-page summary + annotated diagram and a short threat-model appendix, that would be ideal.

Can you confirm a delivery estimate and whether you need any access to our environment to validate assumptions?

Thanks,
Alex Byrne
Lead Information Security Engineer
Cumulus Health

--

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. We can provide: 1) a one-page containment diagram that covers hosted / dedicated / private variants, 2) a short appendix describing KV cache and runtime isolation, and 3) three prioritized threat scenarios with mitigations.

Proposed timeline: draft materials by Tue (2028-05-24) EOD, final deliverables (PDF + annotated PNG + appendix) by Thu (2028-05-26). If that timing looks tight for your review, we can push the final to next Tue (2028-05-30).

We do not need access to your environment to answer these questions; we'll flag any assumptions (e.g., whether you plan to use our Hosted API vs. Redwood Dedicated). If you can confirm which deployment modality Cumulus expects to run in production, we will tailor the diagram accordingly.

Looping in Marcus for the runtime-level details and Laura for network/edge constraints.

Best,
Rachel Kim

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 23 May 2028 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: network containment and tenant isolation for inference workloads

Rachel / Laura — drafting a focused appendix with the following pieces:

- Serving runtime isolation: per-request KV namespaces, GC boundaries, and per-tenant process sandboxes (we'll call out the exact mechanism per deployment variant).
- Memory/KV cache model: runtime maintains per-model per-tenant KV caches; caches are keyed by tenant-id + model id and never shared. We will include pseudocode-like flow to show cache eviction and zeroization on tenant teardown.
- Control plane threat: controller-to-inference plane channel is authenticated via mTLS with mutual cert rotation; we'll enumerate rollback-proofing steps and recommended monitoring.

I'll prepare a small diagram showing runtime layers and annotate the spots where we apply enforced boundaries.

Marcus
Senior Applied ML Engineer — Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Byrne <alex.byrne@cumulus-health.com>
Cc: security.team@cumulus-health.com, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: network containment and tenant isolation for inference workloads

Alex — thanks for the patience. Attached are the deliverables: a one-page containment overview, the annotated topology (PNG), and a short threat-model appendix. Key highlights below — full details are in the attachments/drive link.

Summary highlights:
- Deployment variants: Hosted API uses a multi-tenant fronting layer with strict per-tenant VRF and egress NATting by region; Dedicated uses isolated GPU pools, VPC peering (customer-managed), and optional private egress nodes; Private (VPC/on-prem) places the entire control plane in customer network and removes shared-hosting egress paths.

- Runtime isolation and KV cache: KV caches are namespaced per-tenant and stored in isolated in-memory segments backed by process boundaries. Cache keys include tenant-id; cache eviction includes immediate zeroization for any tenant termination. We do not expose cross-tenant admin endpoints in the runtime; any admin actions require control-plane authorization with RBAC and signed audit entries.

- Lateral movement scenarios (top 3) and mitigations:
  1) Compromised control-plane credentials: mitigations include short-lived certs, mandatory mTLS, step-up auth for sensitive APIs, and real-time anomaly detection + automatic revocation workflows.
  2) Misrouted egress from multi-tenant front-end: mitigations include VRF isolation, strict egress ACLs per-tenant, and per-tenant DNS views.
  3) Side-channel / KV cache data leakage: mitigations include per-tenant cache namespace, memory zeroization on purge, pointer safety checks in native kernels, and scheduled runtime fuzzing.

Attachments / deliverables:
- redwood_network_containment_overview.pdf (one-page summary)
- redwood_kvcache_topology.png (annotated runtime diagram)
- cumulus_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (simple checklist mapping answers to RFI questions)

Drive link for editable originals: https://drive.redwood.company/drive/folders/rdw-cumulus-rfi-2028
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/HD-4729

Rachel Kim
